answer: In PoA's trust graph a cloned fleet betrays itself: many vertices wired densely to each other yet reaching the honest set only across a thin canyon of attestation edges. I score an identity by the min-cut capacity separating it from already-established graders — a narrow cut marks it as a relic of one operator's duplication. Eligibility demands that cut exceed a floor funded by independent cross-attestations, so each extra vertex the attacker adds must buy its own costly bridge.
